basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment and visual dysfunction define disease; strabismus/nystagmus in 3/5; cardiac septal defects in 2/5. Recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.
Congenital fistulae involve lower-lip oral mucosa and sometimes accessory salivary glands; infection is an optional complication.
Hantavirus infection defined by renal injury, thrombocytopenia and hemorrhagic coagulopathy; blurred vision alone does not establish ocular damage.
Septal, eyelid and radial defects define syndrome; anal atresia/malposition in 30-79%. Hearing and additional neurologic abnormalities omitted under the four-axis cap.
Mitochondrial energy-metabolism defects with lactic acidosis and severe developmental/white-matter disease; cardiac and optic damage vary across subtypes; hypotonia alone does not prove myopathy.
Villous epithelial adenoma arises in the appendix.
Mature B-cell lymphoma arising in the mediastinum; lymphoid-cell malignancy supports both mechanism axes. Mediastinal location alone does not establish lung or cardiac invasion.
High-grade glioma arises in central nervous system glial tissue.
Sensorineural deafness and progressive retinal degeneration define Usher syndrome; vestibular dysfunction is otologic. Ataxia does not establish separate CNS damage.
Inherited neurologic channelopathy causing hemiplegic migraine, sometimes with progressive cerebellar dysfunction; visual aura does not indicate eye damage.
Infection directly affects the brain, spinal cord or their coverings.
Limb, heart and cleft-palate defects define syndrome; lung hypoplasia in 80-99%. Auditory-canal, parathyroid and renal abnormalities omitted under the four-axis cap.
Cerebellar injury causes the defining motor coordination disorder.
Cerebellar channelopathy causes episodic ataxia and dysarthria; gaze-evoked nystagmus and vertigo do not establish separate eye or inner-ear damage.
Umbrella disorder of the inner ear; infection is only one possible cause, and associated dizziness or visual symptoms do not establish other organ damage.
Coagulation-factor deficiency defines disease; recurrent hemarthroses cause chronic joint damage in roughly 30% or more over the course, concentrated in moderate/severe disease.
Developmental delay, intellectual disability and frequent seizures define syndrome. Mild clinodactyly/toe syndactyly do not establish substantial locomotor damage.
Primary skeletal myopathy with distal weakness and atrophy; cardiomyopathy is occasional (5-29%). Isolated atrial enlargement in one patient does not establish common cardiac damage.
Lymphatic drainage failure causes persistent skin/subcutaneous edema and tissue remodeling; lymphatic obstruction alone does not establish blood-vessel disease or immune dysfunction.
Isolated oocyte maturation failure causes female infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ involvement is established.
Acquired testicular failure represents gonadal hypofunction, including impaired androgen production; gonads as hormone organs belong to the endocrine axis.
Distal, extraocular/eyelid and pharyngeal myopathy define disease; vocal-cord paresis occurs in 30-79%. Dysphagia is pharyngeal; respiratory muscle weakness alone adds no lung injury.
Carcinoma originates in gastric epithelium; metastatic sites are not defining involvement across the umbrella.
Oxidative-phosphorylation defect with lactic acidosis; hepatic steatosis/enzyme injury and hypotonia with muscle-biopsy abnormalities each in 1/2. Respiratory distress alone adds no pulmonary axis.
Diffuse mucin deposition in skin; the cutaneous mucinosis parent supports skin involvement without establishing systemic organ damage.
